To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new technique for optical frequency dissemination is developed, which can be used for a multi-node system with post automatic correction of the phase noise induced by the fiber link.

we report a technique for the transfer laser light with post phase noise correction, where the optical frequency noise is compensated by the end-users, and we experimentally demonstrate that this technique can be implemented in the real world with a lab-based fiber link.
we report a technique for the coherence transfer of laser frequency through a fiber link with post automatic phase correction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a multi-node optical fiber frequency dissemination system with a post automatic phase noise compensation.
the development of a multi-node optical dissemination system with post-automatic phase noise correction.
the development of a new method for the transfer of coherent light through a fiber network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the technique reported herein is a significant step forward in optical frequency dissemination.
the phase noise of the light after being transferred through a 145 km-long fiber can be corrected to <inline-formula>$10^{-18}$ range with the help of the passive phase noise correction.

we demonstrate a technique to transfer laser light through an arbitrarily long fiber link with a passive remote phase noise correction, where a factor of seven improvement in the residual fiber phase noise and a relative frequency instability at the level of <tex-math notation='LaTeX'>10<sup>-18</sup></tex-math> at 10, 000 s are achieved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrate an open-loop, post automatic phase noise cancellation technique for optical fiber-based phase noise transfer.
the phase noise of the light after fiber transfer is reduced by a factor of 7, compared with that without phase noise compensation.
we propose and demonstrate a novel technique for optical frequency dissemination with post automatic phase correction, which can be used for multi-user applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the optical signal can be transmitted simultaneously and coherently to multiple remote sites, and the phase noise induced by the fiber link can be compensated by remote users without the need for phase discrimination or active phase tracking.

the optical frequency dissemination system can be extended to a multi-node optical fiber network with passive phase noise cancellation, where each node can be equipped with a single laser and a phase noise compensator, without the need for phase discriminators or active phase noise cancellation.
the fiber link phase noise is not a limiting factor in optical frequency dissemination.
